text:
alex: Proposal: switch some tenants to a 'snapshot-on-assign' semantics for prefix ownership. when a worker receives an assignment it records an immutable assign_token for that prefix and uses it for eviction/acceptance checks. should prevent double-evict / reassign races we've been hitting in 2.x canaries.
maria: quick Q — you mean we take a tiny ownership snapshot (token + epoch) and reject operations that don't match the token?
alex: yep. assign flow: allocate token := uuid(), persist token -> worker, worker uses token for lifetime decisions. demote/evict must carry the token to be accepted. if token mismatches, reject and ask orchestrator to re-evaluate.
ken: how is this better than epoch CAS we already have? isn't this similar to lease fencing?
alex: it's close to fencing but explicit and immutable for the assignment window. epochs can increment and still race if reassign happens quickly and in-flight operations use old epoch; token check is stricter because it's bound to that exact assignment.
jamal: downside: extra metadata per prefix in memory + need to thread token into every KV-cache operation. cost estimate?
sasha: +1 on cost concern. but tokens are tiny (16-32B). overhead at 1M prefixes = ~32MB, acceptable. main work is plumbing in the hot path.
maria: what about eviction churn? we need to ensure we don't create permanent rejects that hurt tail latency.
alex: plan: two-phase rollout. 1) implement token check but fallback on mismatch for read-paths (log metric evict_token_mismatch_read), 2) enable strict reject for eviction-only, 3) canary full strictness on 10% tenants.
ken: metrics to observe: prefix_reassign_errors, evict_rejects_due_to_token, assign_latency_ms, prefix_miss_tail_latency_p95. also track retry amplification (ops retried due to mismatch).
jamal: unit tests: interleave assign/reassign + in-flight reads/writes, and a small chaos sim that injects delays between assign and visible token. also an integration test that runs canary config for 1 hour against production-like load.
sasha: example check pseudocode:
```
function accept_op(op, prefix):
  current = prefix.metadata.assign_token
  if op.token != current:
    metric.inc("evict_rejects_due_to_token")
    return reject("stale-token")
  process(op)
```

alex: logs we expect on mismatch (for debugging): `WARN prefix=abc assign_tok=12345 op_tok=67890 op=evict reason=stale-token`
maria: ordering semantics — if orchestrator retries assign after mismatch we must ensure it replays a new token and that previous worker clears live references. add a small gc grace window to avoid flapping.
ken: propose a configurable grace: token_grace_ms default 250ms. during grace, rejects are treated as soft (schedule background recheck) rather than immediate hard evict. can help with network jitter.
jamal: we must update telemetry names and dashboards before enabling strict mode, otherwise alerts will blow up.
sasha: rollout plan: dev env -> staging (100% non-prod tenants) -> production 10% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks if metrics stable. add canary guard: if evict_rejects_due_to_token > 0.5% of evictions OR prefix_miss_tail_latency_p99 increases > 15% -> auto rollback.
alex: implementation tasks: 1) metadata field + persistence change (small migration), 2) hotpath token plumbing + fast path for same-token, 3) metrics + logs, 4) tests + chaos harness, 5) rollout gating.
maria: question: persistence: do we persist token to central control plane or keep ephemeral per-worker?
alex: persist in control plane to allow orchestrator to verify and to recover after worker restart. worker also keeps a local cached token to avoid RPC for every op. if mismatch, orchestrator will reconcile.
ken: potential optimization: use short numeric tokens (monotonic counter per prefix) instead of UUIDs to reduce size in logs and better debugging. but add wrap protection.
jamal: agree on numeric counter with epoch+counter encoding. simpler to reason about in dashboards.
sasha: I'll draft the RFC-followup PR with code sketch, test plan, and rollout checklist.
alex: pairing request: @sasha + @ken on plumbing; @jamal on chaos tests; @maria on rollout gates/alerts.
evict-bot: deploy status: no deploys triggered.
ken: one more thought — make token checks optional per prefix class (hot vs cold) so we can prioritize hot prefixes that cause most churn. config flag `prefix_token_enforcement=hot-only` would help incremental adoption.
alex: good idea. add config to canary matrix.
maria: sounds actionable. I'll own the rollout doc. thanks all :thumbsup:
